prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, which opened the 10^-18 regime of atomic timekeeping and precision measurement

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: a single part, B035, credited to Katori and Ye. The chair asked what physical step makes the lattice clock distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. My answer is the magic-wavelength condition. It makes the light shift on the clock transition vanish to first order, so that many neutral atoms can be held tightly in the Lamb-Dicke regime and interrogated in parallel without Doppler or recoil broadening. That is a different physical mechanism from a single trapped ion, where the statistical advantage of an ensemble is unavailable, and it is not a property of the comb, which only counts optical cycles. Ye's group then showed that the many-body (collisional and lattice-induced) shifts can be controlled and that the lattice gives stability and systematic uncertainty near 1e-18, and independent laboratories now reproduce this. That is the scientific content a citation should name. On the chair's citation question, I would keep both elements, concept and 10^-18 performance, because the two names map onto them, and I would phrase the citation around the lattice clock itself and not around precision spectroscopy in general. The pending redefinition of the second is a supporting consequence for me, not a necessary condition: the clocks already compare routinely across laboratories and are used in tests of constants and relativistic geodesy.
statement.case_against: The overlap reservation remains the strongest, and I do not claim to have removed it, only to have located the new step. Lemonde, Takamoto, the SYRTE, PTB and NIST Sr and Yb groups, and the ion-clock community contributed decisively to the performance records, and a two-name prize cannot express this; the citation wording can only limit the claim to the invention and realisation. The case would also be stronger if the redefinition of the second had already been decided, and a committee that wanted to wait for it would not be unreasonable. Finally, precision measurement is judged less far-reaching than a new class of matter or the Higgs discovery by some colleagues (Mehlig, Danielsson), and I cannot say they are wrong on pure significance; I weigh attribution and checkable maturity more heavily this year.

responses.point: Pearce proposes a second part, B023, crediting Halzen alone for IceCube, and flags this as an attribution compromise because Karle and Spiering are named on the ballot.
responses.response: I accept that the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux is a real discovery and that the instrument is a landmark. But I would not add it as a second part. A one-name credit for a collaboration-scale detector is, as Pearce says himself, a compromise, and the chair's own summary records that no other member supports it. Danielsson's point that the origin of most of the flux is unresolved and that water-based confirmation is incomplete also seems right to me. Adding a second part whose credit we cannot defend would weaken a prize whose first part is clean, and the prize rules do not oblige us to use the third name. I keep IceCube as a candidate for a later year, once source identification and independent confirmation have matured.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B008 for its new organising principle, a rapid decisive HgTe experiment and field-wide consequences, but says he would not defend it against a well-argued shift to B035 because of the credit problem.
responses.response: I agree with his scientific description of B008 and I list it as my first alternative, ahead of circuit QED. The Kane-Mele idea and the Molenkamp experiment are the strongest theory-plus-experiment pairing among the alternatives. My difficulty is the same one he states: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route that was measured, Zhang is deceased, and the three-dimensional work of Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore and Balents, and Hasan lies outside the credit set. Within three names I do not see a citation that does not look narrow or arbitrary. I also do not want the 2016 overlap question to be decided under time pressure. So I would move to B008 only if the committee found a defensible wording, and I do not think it has.

responses.point: Mehlig regards B008 as arguably more far-reaching in science and says he would not want a clean attribution to count for more than the science, while still preferring B035 and treating the unanimity of the two proposed names as information.
responses.response: I take this seriously and it is the right test. Clean credit should not rescue weak science, and I have tried to apply that. The lattice clock passes on the science: a new mechanism, a measured gain of orders of magnitude in uncertainty, independent reproduction and concrete uses. I accept that B008 changes how the field thinks about band structure more than the clocks change how we think about atoms. But a prize must also name people, and where the conceptual case is similar in strength I let the credit decide. On this I differ from Mehlig in weight, not in kind, and I think we agree on the ranking of B035 first.

responses.point: Kroll treats lattice clocks as a new step distinct from the comb and ion-control prizes, and asks whether Ye's credit is for the lattice-clock realisation specifically or for a wider programme in combs, ultracold matter and many-body spectroscopy.
responses.response: I think the answer should be the realisation specifically, and I would draft the citation that way. Ye's relevant contribution is the demonstration of the Sr lattice clock, the control of many-body and systematic shifts, and the 10^-18 result. His earlier comb work belongs to the 2005 recognition and should not count again. Naming the lattice clock in the citation, as I did in round 1, keeps the credit narrow enough to avoid overlap. I would also accept Kroll's earlier suggestion that the citation not lean on the redefinition of the second, since that decision has not yet been made.

responses.point: Danielsson says that circuit QED would be hard to defend a second time so soon after 2025, and that I should treat my own field proximity as a caution; he now also prefers B035 to the Higgs configuration he opened with.
responses.response: I accept the caution and have acted on it. My conflict note on B004 stands, and I think the committee should discount my enthusiasm for it, as Danielsson does, and I would not argue for it this year. I do still hold that circuit QED is conceptually distinct from the macroscopic tunnelling honoured in 2025, since it concerns coupling and readout architecture rather than quantised macroscopic states, and that this distance will matter more as time passes. But on the Girvin and Huang omission I agree with him that the credit is not clean today. This is part of why I keep it as an alternative and not as my choice.

uncertainties: Whether colleagues accept that the magic-wavelength lattice with many-atom Lamb-Dicke interrogation is a distinct enough step from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes.
Whether the contributions of Lemonde, Takamoto and the Sr and Yb groups at SYRTE, PTB and NIST change a two-person allocation, and whether citation wording alone can handle this.
Whether the redefinition of the second, if decided soon, would turn a strong case into an unarguable one, and whether waiting a year or two is the better course.
Whether any wording for B008 within three names could handle Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the three-dimensional work, and whether the 2016 overlap is as limited as Eriksson argues.
I rely on my general knowledge for the clock accuracy records and the priority history and have not verified them beyond the supplied shortlist.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. Circuit QED (B004) is my own research field (circuit and waveguide QED, superconducting qubits), I direct WACQT, which builds on the cQED architecture, and Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson work in the area; Olsson, who is also at Chalmers, has raised the same point. The profile records no personal tie to Blais, Wallraff or Schoelkopf. I propose B004 only as a lower alternative and my views on it should be weighed with this interest in mind; I would accept recusal from any deliberation specific to B004. I record no specific conflict for B035, B008 or B023.
